statement: A sequence is defined by $u_{1}=1$ and $u_{n+1}=2u_{n}+1$ for $n\ge1$. Find a formula for $u_{n}$ and prove it by induction.
solution:
Computing the first few terms: $1,3,7,15,\dots$ suggests $u_{n}=2^{n}-1$.
Proof by induction: for $n=1$, $u_{1}=1=2^{1}-1$, true.
Assume $u_{k}=2^{k}-1$. Then
$$u_{k+1}=2u_{k}+1=2(2^{k}-1)+1=2^{k+1}-2+1=2^{k+1}-1,$$
so the formula holds for $k+1$. By induction, $u_{n}=2^{n}-1$ for all $n\ge1$.
hints: Work out the first four terms to spot the pattern.
Use the recurrence in the induction step.
